finding.summary: Design doc now asserts a blanket "a dry run never reaches the network" contract, but six sibling read commands outside the diff still fetch under --dry-run
finding.evidence: The change is accompanied by docs/design/cli.md:824-827 ("Reads honour the flag too … A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless"), and the new test header repeats it. That universal claim is false for the read commands the diff did not touch, all of which call the client with no `opts.dryRun` guard: packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:40 (`slides list`), slides.ts:81 (`slides get`), packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35 (`notes list`), notes.ts:76 (`notes get`), packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:85 (`files list`), files.ts:105 (`files get`), and packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:39 (`sheets export`, which issues GET /cells before writing the file). An agent that reads the new doc sentence and pre-flights `slides list --dry-run` or `sheets export … --dry-run` still hits the API — and `sheets export` additionally writes the output file. Fix belongs either on those call sites or on the new doc wording (narrow it to the four commands actually changed).

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. docs/design/cli.md:824-827 does state the blanket "A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log" contract alongside the four commands that were given guards (docs.ts:78-83, docs.ts:125-128). Seven sibling read entry points reached by the same global --dry-run option (registered at commands/root.ts:75, exposed via getGlobalOpts) call the client with no dryRun branch: slides.ts:40, slides.ts:81, notes.ts:35, notes.ts:76, files.ts:85, files.ts:105, and sheets-export.ts:39. The inconsistency is internal to those same files (slides.ts guards create/rename/delete/content/export at 60/94/112/141/197; notes.ts at 55/89; files.ts at 118), so the reads are demonstrably bypassing the pattern rather than intentionally exempt. sheets-export.ts is worse than a mere fetch: after the unguarded GET at line 39 it writes the output file at line 51, so `sheets export ... --dry-run` performs a real local write. This is a violated invariant/asserted contract that consumers outside the diff break — the blast-radius lane — and the impact (network calls, rate limit, access-log entries, and a filesystem write under a flag documented as inert) is major. No guard elsewhere prevents these paths: the client layer has no dry-run awareness (client/dry-run.ts only exposes printDryRun, invoked per-command).
